chunk_findings.detail: In `test_a_repeat_of_a_closed_finding_is_the_same_id`, `parse(...)` returns a tuple/list whose first element is the list of findings and whose second element is the boolean `on_contract` flag (as evidenced by line 56: `findings, on_contract = parse(...)`). Therefore, `parse(...)[0]` evaluates to the list of findings, not a single finding object, so indexing it again with `[0]` (`first[0]`) raises an `IndexError: list index out of range` or `TypeError` because it attempts to index the finding object (or fails when `parse(...)[0]` is empty if it returns the list). This breaks the test suite when executed.

chunk_findings.detail: `cut_text` claims a character cut on a line boundary, but `at = at if at > 0 else chars` slices mid-line when `rfind` is -1 or 0. Input `"\n" + ("y"*50)`, `chars=10`, `lines=60`: the newline at index 0 is discarded and `kept` is the first 10 characters (`\nyyyyyyyy`), not a whole line. A single line longer than `chars` is likewise split in the middle.
